coachingNotes.title: Weekly Emphasis Notes
points: The first exercise is crucial to teach the correct body mechanics for passing and receiving. Make sure you demonstrate the correct body mechanics and insist that players execute it correctly. Read the details in the attachment.
The 3V1 exercise is crucial to teach possession. Make sure players are executing each of the four moments of the cycle of possession. Three touches minimum on the ball is required.

The third exercises were skipped last week because we lacked space and time, since we went indoors. Make sure you walk through those exercises in your initial demonstration so players understand and execute them correctly.

coachingNotes.title: Cycle Of Possession
points: This week we continue the microcycle focused on passing and receiving. Start by asking the players to recite the four stages of the cycle of possession:

Get open – pop away from the defender to create time and space (Questions to ask: Who should pop away? Answer: the player off the ball. How many? Everyone except the player with the ball. How often? Every time the ball moves.)
Good first touch (it should be a small touch, turning away from pressure to create time and space and set up a change in the point of attack)

Escape the pressure from a defender by dribbling to space (the ball attracts defenders, so you must escape to create time and space and make a safe pass). Four ways to do this, depending on how close the defender is: touch to the side, skill move, turn and face away, sole delay.
Accurate pass (No matter what you must pass to the feet. The pass must be on the ground and sharp – no slow balls. Pass to the player with the most time and space).
Passing and receiving involves parts 2 and 4 of the cycle of possession. They still must perform 1 and 3, but the focus of your coaching should be 2 and 4.

coachingNotes.title: Key Technical Points
points: Plant the non-kicking foot side-by-side with the ball – make sure they don’t plant it behind the ball.
Turn the knee and toes of the kicking foot to the side, at a 90 degree angle, and point the toe up.
Make contact with the ball only with the solid flat side of the heel, not the side of the big toe.
Turn on the 1st touch every time.
Soft, short 1st touch.
Push through the ball when passing with exaggerated follow-through so you guide the ball to the target accurately.  Control the direction of the pass by swinging your kicking let toward the target.

coachingNotes.title: Important Technical And Tactical Points To Emphasize
points: At this stage never allow 1 touch play during games or game like exercises. It is ok to do 1 touch in warmup exercises after two-touches, as a challenge. Players must learn to make a soft, short 1st touch so they can keep possession and play the ball quickly, rather than blasting the ball away with one touch. That is the biggest reason for turnovers by lower skill players.
When receiving or passing with the inside of the foot make sure your toes are pointing up (so the ball does not pop up or roll over your foot)
When receiving or passing with the outside of the foot point your toe down (same reason…)
When passing, push through the ball and swing the kicking leg up – do not jab the kicking foot down on the ground.

Before receiving pop away and turn your body to open yourself up to face the field of play, and to face your team mates, so you can pass before you are under pressure. This gives you more time and space.
After passing move to space to give your team mates passing options.

Emphasize the cycle of possession: Pop away, good first touch (one that creates time and space); escape the pressure (to create time and space to pass); accurate pass (to the player with the most time and space)

The cue to make a run is when the player with the ball takes a preparation touch and looks up. The cue to pass is when the runner starts the run. So the run comes first. Otherwise always pass to the feet. When passing to the runner pass so the ball meets the feet as well…
Attackers must always be aware what options the defenders are taking away, and what options they are giving you. Take what they give you.
Start making these coaching points with the warmup exercises, and carry them over throughout the progression.

coachingNotes.title: Learning New Skill Moves
points: It is critical that all players learn the basic skills/moves covered this week.  Don't expect them to learn all the moves on the first try. It will take time and many practices. These moves should be part of every pre-game warmup. By the end of the season we expect all players to be able to do each move accurately and with speed.

These moves start by pulling the ball backwards or to the side (to get it out of the defender's reach) and then turning so you are not facing the defender. Players can then dribble away to escape from the defender's pressure.

You must demonstrate each move correctly, or play the videos linked to below (a tablet has a nice large screen). The objective is for every player to master these moves and be able to successfully execute them in a game situation. Players should be able to beat a defender 9 out of 10 times in a game situation. So they need to master the mechanics of the move, be able to execute them against a defender, and to time it correctly. They need to be able to change direction and change speed in order to get out of pressure and create time and space for themselves. Of course this will take time and many repetitions.

coachingNotes.title: Cycle of Possession
points: In the coming weeks we will continue the focus on dribbling. We will do some technical repetitions, but will work in the context of 1v1, 2v1 and other possession games, where the focus will be dribbling to escape the pressure from a defender, and to create enough time and space to make a safe pass or to get a shot. You should continue to instruct your players on the four stages of the cycle of possession (pop away from the defender to create time and space, good first touch when you receive the ball, escape the pressure to create time and space to pass, accurate pass to the feet, and repeat the entire sequence).

coachingNotes.title: How To Beat A Defender
points: The approach: dribble with quick small touches, crouched down (ready to spring) and with your eyes ahead.
The move: Fake in one direction to make the defender commit that way (two or more fakes may be required to make the defender commit)
Change direction in the opposite way
Change speed (accelerate away)

coachingNotes.title: Description Of The Four Basic Moves
points: 1: Hook turn: Using the sole of the foot on top of the ball, turn 180 degrees. If you use the right foot turn counterclockwise. If you use the left foot turn clockwise. In other words, keep turning in the direction you are already going as the foot moves toward the ball. The turn should be lightning fast.

2: Pull-push: This move has three parts. First, fake that you will shoot the ball, but instead put your toes on top of the ball. Second, using the sole of the foot pull the ball backwards, and turn your body 90 degrees (to the right if using the right foot, or to the left if using the left foot). Third, push the ball away with the inside of the same foot. This is a 90 degree move, drawing the letter "L".

3: Pull-cut: Similar to the pull-push, this has three parts. First, fake the shot. Second, using the bottom of the toes (sole) pull the ball back behind the standing leg. Third, using the inside of the same foot cut the ball 90 degrees behind the standing leg.
4: Scissors: Take a leap to the side moving the foot in front of the ball. Push the ball in the opposite directions using the outside of the other foot.

5. Maradona: This combines the hood turn, then the drag-back. First do a hook turn with one foot. Second, do a drag back with the other foot. Keep spinning in the direction you are already going. Do the move in both directions.

coachingNotes.title: Technique Coaching Points
points: Players must use the correct technique when dribbling and taking on defenders: take small soft touches with the shoe laces (point your toe straight down). Quick feet and small steps so you can react quickly. Make the defender react to you, not the other way around. Dribble diagonally several yards to get the defender to move laterally, then you can use the defender's momentum against her or him by changing direction and changing speed.

Players must use the correct technique when passing (contact the ball with the inside of the heel, push through the ball and swing the kicking leg up – do not jab at the ball, or jab your kicking foot into the ground).

Players must use the correct technique when receiving the ball – small touch so you can play it immediately. Use the correct surface of the foot – inside of the heel, or sole of the foot if you are in a tight space.

coachingNotes.title: League Objectives
points: Fun: Your personality, mood, body language, and demeanor are key. Have fun, interact with the players, be positive and kind, be a good listener. Recognize and reward effort rather than game results.
Development: Be prepared, give them specific instructions, help them learn their positions during the game's four moments (attack, defense, transition to defense, transition to attack). Stay active.

Be an active (but positive) coach – give players feedback and instructions while they play, before they substitute in, and after they substitute out. Focus on two or three important things. Too much information is confusing and leads to mental shut-down.
Teach them the positional number system (see below).

coachingNotes.title: Demonstration-Observation-Correction Cycle
points: You must demonstrate each skill move to your players, and then have them repeat them 20 times.
Do not talk while demonstrating. Just do the skill move yourself at game speed, with no talking. Just do the move like you want them to do it in a game situation.
Have the players repeat it 20 times and observe them. Players sit down when done.
Demonstrate again – do it at speed. Then break it down into its two or three component parts. Here you can explain each part, but be brief.
Have the players repeat the skill move 20 times and sit down when done.

So the process is as follows: demonstrate, observe the players, demonstrate again to make corrections, observe the players, and repeat this process until the players' performance improves. Not all players will master every move on the first session. It will take several sessions.
Repeat this for each skill move.
Work on five or six skill moves each practice session, and make sure the players are using those specific moves in the exercise progression for that day.
Our objective is for all players, regardless of their athletic ability, to master every one of these skill moves.

coachingNotes.title: Session Model
points: We are using a progression model for our practice sessions. We will not use the Play-Practice-Play session model, so don't use that. You can still apply the guided discovery technique within the progression model.

coachingNotes.title: Cycle of Possession
points: Most of these are possession games, and you must focus your coaching points on dribbling to escape the pressure from a defender, so you create enough time and space to make a safe pass or to get a shot.

You should all start introducing your players to the four stages of the cycle of possession (1 - pop away from the defender to create time and space, 2- good first touch when you receive the ball, 3 - escape the pressure to create time and space to pass, 4 - accurate pass to the feet, and repeat the entire sequence).

coachingNotes.title: Technique Coaching Points
points: Players must use the correct technique when receiving or dribbling: take small soft touches. Quick feet and small steps so you can react quickly. Dribble side to side, not forward into pressure. Always be aware what spaces the defenders are taking away and what spaces they are giving you. Take what they give you. Shield the ball when necessary.

Players must use the correct technique when passing (contact the ball with the inside of the heel, push through the ball and swing the kicking leg up – do not jab at the ball, or jab your kicking foot into the ground).

Players must use the correct technique when receiving the ball – small touch so you can play it immediately. Use the correct surface of the foot – inside of the heel, or sole of the foot if you are in a tight space.

1v1-end-line-game.title: 1v1 End Line Game
1v1-end-line-game.setup: 10X20 yard area. One group of players with a ball each on one corner. A group of players on the far corner.
instructions: The players in the front of each line move to the center. Blue player passes to red player. They play 1v1 until the ball goes out of bounds. The player with the ball scores by dribbling with control past the opposite end line. The defender must either win the ball and score by dribbling past the opposite end line, or by forcing the attacker out of bounds (no point for either player). Game over when the ball is out of bounds, and the two players go to the opposite lines. The next two players immediately start their battle.
coachingPoints: Accurate pass to the feet.
Good first touch (soft, short touch).
The attacker must start doing fakes immediately – no not wait for the defender to close you down.
Beating a defender: approach the defender with control and doing fakes, fake one way, change direction, change speed (attack the space with maximum speed).

1v1-small-area.title: 1V1 Small Area
1v1-small-area.setup: Area is 8 yards deep and 10 yards wide. Two small goals near the sides. One line of players with balls, one line of players with no balls.
instructions: 1v1 battle starts with an accurate pass to the feet. The receiver must perform one of the three moves in order to score. If the defender wins the ball he now tries to score, but must also perform one of the three moves, or combinations of moves.
coachingPoints: Take a small first touch and do a move immediately.
Do not wait for the defender to close you down.
You may have to do multiple combinations of moves.
Keep the ball moving, and when you see that you have unbalanced the defender accelerate to the side and shoot.
If you lose the ball get goalside quickly.

2v2-1-1-game-2-large-goals.title: 2v2+1+1... Game 2 Large Goals
2v2-1-1-game-2-large-goals.setup: 30X30 yard area with two large goals. The coach has a supply of balls.
instructions: The coach passes the ball to the center, toward one team.
The attacking team overlaps: the far player takes the ball and dribbles diagonally toward the coach.
The player near the coach overlaps to the far side.
THE TEAM IN POSSESSION CAN HAVE ONE EXTRA PLAYER, so they can turn and pass a teammate in.
That makes it 3v2.
If the defenders win the ball they can pass two players in, making it 4v3. Etc.
coachingPoints: Dribble and pass with the correct technique.
Don't wait for the defender to close you down - pass early.
Get a numbers advantage by passing someone in early.
Priority: 1. shoot; 2. pass; 3. dribble.
Create width and depth when attacking.

2v2-2-target-players.title: 2v2 + 2 Target Players
2v2-2-target-players.setup: 20X20 yard area. 3 teams of 2 players. One team serves as target players, outside opposite ends.
instructions: Play 2v2 in the middle.
The team in possession scores by passing to the outside target players, receiving the ball back, and passing to the opposite target player without losing possession.
When a team scores 3 points the losing team becomes target players.
coachingPoints: Escape the pressure by dribbling to the side.
Look up and scan the field to find your team mate.
Pass to the feet.
Turn on the 1st touch.
Move off the ball to get open.
Create maximum width.
When you play to the target both inside players must move wide to create time and space.
One defender MUST try to win the ball when it is played to a target player (can go outside the box), and the target player must take a touch to the side to escape the pressure.
Target players must move laterally to provide safe passing angles.

2v2-game.title: 2V2 Game
2v2-game.setup: 20X30 yard area (adjust for your age group)
instructions: The coach passes to the far corner. The receiver dribbles diagonally, and his team mate overlaps. Two defender come in. Play is continuous until the ball is out of bounds. Goalies are not allowed to punt or shoot.
coachingPoints: Dribble diagonally to create time and space. Pass early. Shoot early. Quick transitions to defense and to offense.
Look to combine with give-&-gos, overlaps, and through balls.
Be aware what the defender is taking away and what he is giving you. Take what he gives you.

3-1-v-1-pass-and-support.title: 3+1 V 1 - Pass And Support
3-1-v-1-pass-and-support.setup: 15x20 yard area, with a buffer zone in the middle. 3v1 on one side, 1 target player on the other. Set up two or three of these so the whole team plays.
instructions: Play 3v1 possession.
Players must make a minimum of 4 passes (more or less as needed) before they can play a long ball to the target player.
The defender then chases the ball to the other side, and two attacking players must then run to the opposite side to support their target player.
They try to get 4 passes and send a long pass the other way again.
They get a point for successfully passing to the target player.
The defender gets a point by winning the ball and passing to the target player.
Change defenders when any group gets three points.
VARIATION: 4V2 + 1 target.
coachingPoints: Move off the ball to provide passing options - safe angle and maximum distance.
Don't force the pass - be patient and make safe passes, until it is safe to pass to the target.

derived.areaSize: 15x20 yards, with a buffer zone in the middle

3v1-possession-game.title: 3v1 Possession Game
3v1-possession-game.setup: 10X10 yard squares. As many squares as needed so all players participate. 3 attackers vs 1 defender.
instructions: Play 3v1 until attackers or defenders get three points.
Attackers score every 5 consecutive passes.
Defenders score by dribbling out of the square through one side designated by the coach.
coachingPoints: Take a touch to the side before passing to create space.
Pass to the feet.
Whenever a pass is made the third attacker must run to provide a passing option on the right or left of the ball.
Pass to the player with the most time and space.
Turn on the 1st touch.
Use deception (fakes).

basic-ball-skills.title: Basic Ball Skills
basic-ball-skills.setup: Individual ball skills – Open area or 20x20 yard area, no need to use a line of cones. The coach demonstrates each move, players repeat it 10 times. Note that in the videos linked some of the moves are given a different name. A rose by any other name… Spend 10 minutes on this. If you do all the list below it will take you more than an hour… After players learn all the moves they can do more of them inside of 10 minutes.
instructions: Side step https://youtu.be/-pwFS7tg16E
Scissors https://youtu.be/QpLPYdHlGGs
Step-Overs https://youtu.be/cldbJhHK0Ks
Cruyff https://youtu.be/RQFs_no6MGs
Twist (shimmy) https://youtu.be/0fQx2l8Q_uM
Pull-push https://youtu.be/mB0G4lHSSyI
Pull-cut https://youtu.be/-dNzgYSBQi8
Hook turn (called U turn in the video) https://youtu.be/n4FaeICzPtM
Drag back – 180 degree turn, drag ball straight back using sole of foot, turn body right if using right foot, left if using left foot
Maradona https://youtu.be/DzbdeHLbxwg
Sole delay (and pop away to the side) https://youtu.be/IlgdHkqkzjI
Full circle, 360 degrees circle (three touches is enough to do a full circle; chop the ball around using the inside of the foot, then outside of the foot, then repeat with the other foot)
coachingPoints: These points refer to when and why players must each of these skill moves in a game: to create time and space for themselves and escape the pressure from a defender.

Any time you have the ball there will be a defender right in front of you. You must dribble to the side in order to escape the pressure. There are four basic ways to do this: cut to the side, turn and face away, sole delay, and skill moves. Choose the right way depending on how close the defender is to you.
If you have lots of space between you and the defender: use skill moves like the scissors or step-overs

If you have a couple yards between you and the defender: use the twist, pull-push, pull-cut, sole delay, Maradona. But the fastest and safest way to escape pressure in this situation is a simple cut to the side.
If the defender is really close you must TURN AND FACE AWAY immediately. Use the inside cut, Cruyff, hook turn, or dragback

dribble-skill-pass-1.title: Dribble-Skill-Pass 1
dribble-skill-pass-1.setup: Several lines with 3 cones each so you have 3 players per line. If your team has 12 players you will need 4 lines. Cones are 10 yards apart. One ball per line. Two players on one side, one player on the other.
instructions: The player with the ball dribbles with the laces toward the middle cone, performs a designated skill move, takes a touch to the side, and passes to the opposite player.
He then follows the pass and runs to the opposite side.
The receiver does a good first touch, and repeats the process in the other direction.
coachingPoints: Dribble with the laces, toes pointing down, small quick touches.
Do the designated move early - don't get too close to the middle cone (=defender).
Take a touch straight to the side to create space to pass.
Make an accurate pass (swing your passing leg straight toward the target player).
Spring to the opposite line (take the place of the receiver).
Skills: 1. touch to the side; 2. side step; 3. scissors; 4. step-over; 5. Iniesta; 6. pull-push; 7. pull-cut

derived.areaSize: cones set 10 yards apart per line

dribbling-four-goals.title: Dribbling - Four Goals
instructions: The coach plays a diagonal ball toward the far goal. The attacker runs behind the far goal. The defender runs behind the near goal. Switch roles after all players have gone a turn.
1: Score by dribbling through.
2: Score by shooting.
coachingPoints: Attackers: Get to the ball first. Take a first touch toward one of the goals to make the defender commit to that goal. Then quickly turn and attack the opposite goal.

Defenders: Get to the ball as quickly as possible to deny the shot. Don't stab at it, or dive in. Instead, delay the attack by staying on your toes and shuffling to keep the ball in front of you. Be patient and wait for the attacker to make a mistake. If you win the ball counterattack quickly.

dribbling-gauntlet.title: Dribbling Gauntlet

diagram.extractedFrom: page-1 FlateDecode /Image XObject (raw pixels, re-packed as PNG)

dribbling-gauntlet.setup: 10X36 yard area, divided into three 10X12 sections. Three defenders, and a line of attackers.
instructions: One attacker dribbles through and scores by dribbling past the last end line. On the way the attacker must beat each defender.

Defenders must start at the back line of their respective squares. Defenders are not allowed outside their respective squares. Defenders score by winning the ball and stopping the ball dead on the front line of their square.
coachingPoints: Dribble with shoelaces to take on defenders. Make your move early, out of the defender's reach.
Change direction, and accelerate away.
Attack the spaces behind the defender with speed.
Control the ball again when you enter the next square.

dribbling-multiple-gates.title: Dribbling - Multiple Gates
dribbling-multiple-gates.setup: 30X40 area (adjust to your # of players and age). Multiple "gates" made with cones.
instructions: Play multiple 1V1 battles. Dribbler scores by dribbling through gates. Defender must deny the dribble through the gates, but cannot steal the ball. Play 1 or 2 minutes, and switch roles. Keep score.
Variation 2: Defenders can win the ball. Keep score.
coachingPoints: Take soft short touches, keeping the ball "tied" to your feet. Quick choppy steps, with constant changes of direction.
The objective is to be unpredictable and to move the ball before the defender can react.
Make the defender commit to defend one gate, and immediately change directions to another gate.
Use every surface of both feet.

derived.areaSize: 30x40 yards (adjust to # of players and age)

dynamic-stretching.title: Dynamic Stretching
instructions: Skipping lap
High kneesButt-kickers
Carioca
Forward lunge
Side lunge
Side squat
Knee to chest
Airplane
Toe touch
High kick
coachingPoints: Dynamic Stretching (Ex: https://youtu.be/G2HRt2-wZ-s)

multiple-1v1s-dribble-pass.title: Multiple 1v1s - Dribble-Pass
multiple-1v1s-dribble-pass.setup: 20x20 or 20x30 area. Two teams. Target players for each team on opposite sides, multiple 1v1 pairs inside.
instructions: Players keep the ball away from the defender, and pass to the target player outside. The target player and the passer switch positions and the defender keeps following the same ball.
coachingPoints: Player with the ball: Never face the defender - turn and dribble out. Pass early. Accurate passes to the feet. Call out the target's name to make sure she is ready.
Target: Good first touch into open space. Accelerate away and pass to the target player on the opposite side. Pass from a distance, so you don't bring the defender close to the target.

passing-body-mechanics.title: Passing - Body Mechanics
passing-body-mechanics.setup: Two cones 3 or 4 feet apart forming a gate. Two players and one ball on either side. Set up multiple gates so all players participate simultaneously.
instructions: Variation 1: Players pass back and forth, each player must take two touches.
Variation 2: Race - see which pair of players can complete 40 passes first (repeat).
Variation 3: Players pass back and forth, each player has only one touch.
Variation 4: Race - see which pair of players can complete 40 passes first (repeat).
coachingPoints: Make sure all players are using the right body mechanics/body shape.
They must perform this correctly to develop good habits.
This is the right body mechanics: 1. Plant the non kicking foot side by side with the ball (not behind it), with the toes pointing to the target player.
2. Point the non kicking foot and knee to the side, 90 degrees in relation to the non kicking foot.

3. Swing the kicking foot through the ball and up in the air, like a golf put. Do not fall forward and jab your kicking foot into the ground. Swing the leg in a straight line directly toward the target.
3. Contact the ball with the flat side of the heel, not the side of the big toe.
Coaches must make sure all players perform with the correct body mechanics.

possession-knockout-game.title: Possession Knockout Game
instructions: Team in possession has two or three balls. Two "sharks" go after the ball. You can stipulate that the sharks cannot double team.
coachingPoints: Escape the pressure from the defender quickly. Pass early. Accurate passes to the feet.
Players off the ball must create time and space.
